title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
publication_status_observed: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2021; arXiv preprint arXiv:2010.01412v3
main_claims: SAM improves model generalization by simultaneously minimizing training loss value and loss sharpness via a min-max optimization problem solved efficiently with two gradient computations per iteration.
SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and finetuning tasks when applied to a broad range of architectures.
m-sharpness (sharpness computed per small data subset) better correlates with actual generalization gap than full-training-set sharpness, and smaller m yields better generalization.
methodology: SAM formulates a PAC-Bayes-motivated generalization bound that includes a neighborhood-wise training loss term. The inner maximization is approximated via a first-order Taylor expansion, solved in two gradient computations per iteration. Experiments span CIFAR-10/100 with WideResNets, PyramidNets, ImageNet with ResNets, finetuning of EfficientNet models, and noisy-label classification, all using 5 independent random seeds.
key_results: SAM reduces WideResNet-28-10 test error from 3.5% to 2.7% on CIFAR-10 (basic augmentation, 200 epochs) and from 18.8% to 16.5% on CIFAR-100.
SAM improves ResNet-152 ImageNet top-1 error from 20.3% to 18.4% at 400 epochs.
SAM model trained with SAM reaches λmax ≈1.0 at convergence vs ≈24 without SAM for a WideResNet on CIFAR-10, confirming reduced curvature.
limitations: SAM requires approximately twice the computational cost of base optimizers due to two gradient computations per step.
The PAC-Bayes generalization bound relies on assumptions (e.g., Gaussian perturbation does not decrease test error) that may not hold universally.
Second-order terms are dropped in the gradient approximation; including them was found to degrade performance in initial experiments.
relevance_to_rq: This is the foundational SAM paper central to the RQ. It establishes the SAM formulation (ρ=0.05 default for ResNet+CIFAR), provides the Hessian spectrum evidence that SAM finds flatter minima, and introduces m-sharpness. The RQ directly asks whether SAM's OOD gains are explained by this flatness mechanism or by representation stability — this paper is the origin point of the flatness explanation.
